messages:
maria: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a 'trace sweep' aggregator for nightly CI to automatically collect nsys / perfetto traces for kernel-selection / batching / KV-cache regression detection. Need quick feedback on retention, sampling rules, and what the diff dashboard should prioritize.
jason: SGTM. what's the target artifact budget? S3 costs are the main limiter here.
maria: Goal: ~1000 candidates/day but actually persist ~200 stratified samples (by model, seq_len_bucket, kernel_variant). Expected ~50–200 MB/day compressed. We can tighten if cost spikes.
sam: Strong +1 for deterministic sample seeds and deterministic inputs so diffs are meaningful. Also explicitly capture KV-cache warmup traces (first 5 iters) and a steady-state trace (after 100 iters).
lia: Agree on KV warmup. Also we should capture per-kernel perf counters (e.g., sm_efficiency, l2_miss_rate) and CUDA context stats. Example nsys invocation I'm testing:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --sample=none --stats=true \
  -o /tmp/trace.$JOB_ID nsys_target_binary --model redwood-v1-small --seq 1024
```
We stash the .qdrep and export a perfetto json for flamegraphs.
jason: For retention: raw traces -> 7 days in warm S3, then glacier/deep archive at 30 days. Indexed summaries (metadata + thumbnails) keep 180 days. Also add budget alarms.
ci-bot: ci-bot: nightly-trace-sweep triggered for matrix: model=redwood-v1-small,sequence=1024,kernel=auto. job=trace-agg-2246789012 queued.
maria: Index structure proposal: store a small per-trace metadata row (flat json blob) with fields: hash, model, seq_len_bucket, batch_size, kernel_variant, host, runtime_version, nsys_version, kv_warmup_flag, perfetto_id, size_bytes. Push that into ES/Dynamo for fast query. Keep raw path as s3://redwood-ci-traces/YYYY/MM/DD/<hash>.qdrep.gz.
sam: Add regression detection heuristics: compare per-kernel p50/p95 against baseline window (last 14 days) and flag any kernel where p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.15 AND sample_count > 3. Also require same input seed to reduce noise.
jason: Dashboard: need a 'diff by kernel' view with small flamegraph overlay + table of counters (invocations, avg latency, p95, mem_bw). We can link to trace thumbnails and a raw-download button. Maybe proto at https://dash.redwood/internal/traces-diff (placeholder).
lia: Important: traces may contain user inputs. We must scrub prompt text before uploading. Store only hashed inputs + masked prompt placeholders. Also enforce SSE-KMS and bucket-level access controls.
maria: Action items: I'll open PR for trace-collector lambda + upload script (trace/ci-sweep-indexer). @sam to prototype diff comparator and threshold config. @jason to scope S3 lifecycle + cost alerting. @lia to provide scrubber util + security signoff. ETA EOW?
sam: I can get a comparator prototype by Thursday, will include a small C++/py tool to diff kernel timelines and compute per-op regressions.
jason: I'll configure lifecycle rules + budget alerts and share numbers. Ping me in-thread when PR lands.
ci-bot: ci-bot: trace-agg-2246789012 started on runner r-42. logs: "captured 48 traces, total 34MB gzipped, uploaded 48 metadata rows".
maria: :thumbsup: branch trace/ci-sweep-indexer created. Putting sample selection rules and baseline snapshot strategy in the PR description.
